notes: Wallclock bounds in milliseconds, one per task class, and this file is their only home — no per-seat timeout prose lives anywhere else. The bounds are deliberately generous per the operator's ruling: a worker is never killed for thinking, only for hanging, so thirty and forty-five minute bounds are correct where the class warrants them. FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE CODEX DISPATCH WRAPPER: enforcing codex_dispatch means killing a real process tree, and the kill sweep must enumerate BY THE RECORDED CODEX SESSION ID. setsid makes the dispatched child a session leader, and codex spawns its MCP servers into sibling process groups inside that same session, so a plain PGID kill leaves them running. Never match on process name.
